research_question: What is the effect of zinc compared with placebo on the duration of the common cold in people with a naturally acquired cold?
outcome_description: Mean duration of the common cold in days from start of treatment or symptom onset to resolution
positive_direction: Shorter duration of cold symptoms (favoring zinc over placebo)
search_queries: zinc common cold duration clinical trial
zinc lozenges cold symptoms randomized controlled trial
zinc treatment common cold days to resolution trial
inclusion_criteria: Empirical clinical trials evaluating zinc (oral lozenges, tablets, or intranasal preparations) compared to placebo in individuals with naturally acquired common cold
Studies reporting quantitative outcome data on the mean duration of the common cold in days from treatment start or symptom onset to resolution
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, and narrative reviews are excluded)
No comparison between zinc and a placebo or control group
No quantitative outcome data allowing calculation of an effect size for cold duration (e.g., missing means, SDs, SEs, or equivalent statistics)

Unrelated to the research question, including prevention/prophylaxis studies, experimentally induced/inoculated colds, or studies reporting only symptom severity scores or adverse events without cold duration
moderators_to_extract: Zinc formulation and route (e.g., zinc acetate lozenges, zinc gluconate lozenges, tablets, intranasal)
Time from cold symptom onset to treatment initiation (e.g., <24 hours vs ≥24 hours)
Trial definition and criteria for cold resolution
effect_size_note: Mean difference (MD) in days to resolution of common cold symptoms between zinc and placebo groups.
